119447.name: Bais Chana Girls High School
119447.note: The Chabad Chinuch Office's Directory of Chabad Educational Institutions (2012-13 edition, high schools): 'Bais Chana High School, Principal: Mrs. Chanie Fogelman, 15 Midland St., Worcester, MA 01602 ... Founded 1972, 7-12'. A directory's year, so medium. Chabad.org (on CrownHeights.info, 5 Nov 2025): after 1947 'The couple later founded a girls' high school, which the Rebbe asked to be named Bais Chana'. Worcester Telegram (on CrownHeights.info, 7 Feb 2011): about 30 girls 'attending the girls' Bais Chana High School at 15 Midland St.' Its chabad.org listing is in the first online directory (listings published July 22 2004), so it existed by then.

119975.name: Food & Learning Center
119975.note: David M. Noel, 'A History of the Toledo Jewish Community 1895-2006' (p. 156; its Chabad section is from a document Rabbi Shemtov sent the author): 'In 1993 the "Food and Learning Center" opened, catering to the "financial, emotional and spiritual need of new Americans in our community, although its outreach is available to all those in the Toledo Jewish community."' Nothing found (Toledo Blade and Toledo Jewish News searched). Its chabad.org listing is in the first online directory (listings published July 22 2004), so it existed by then.

120080.name: Gan Chaya Jewish Early Childhood Center
120080.note: Yelp's business line (647 S Saltair Ave): 'Established in 2004. Gan Chaya was created off of the strong yearning to provide children with proper education in a natural setting.' Only Yelp, so medium; it fits its chabad.org listing, up by July 22 2004. Mrs. Channa Hecht's preschool (Chabad of Brentwood is from 1985). It is in chabad.org's first directory (its listing went up July 22 2004, when that directory was put online), so it ran by then; in 2008 it was at 1620 S. Bundy Dr., where Chabad of Brentwood South held its first services (Chabad of Brentwood's site, archived June 30 2008). Now 647 S. Saltair Ave. Not in the Chinuch Office's 2012-13 preschool directory. Its chabad.org listing is in the first online directory (listings published July 22 2004), so it existed by then. Mrs. Channa Hecht has held a license for a family child care home in Los Angeles since Sept 6 2018 ('Hecht Family Child Care', facility 197493559; the state does not publish home addresses), and the listing now gives 647 S. Saltair Ave., a house, so the Gan may now run as her licensed home daycare; no preschool license at 1620 S. Bundy Dr. is in the state's data (which keeps closed ones only from 2020).

119974.name: Gan Yeladim Preschool
119974.note: David M. Noel, 'A History of the Toledo Jewish Community 1895-2006' (p. 156, from Rabbi Shemtov's own account): 'In 1992, Raizel Shemtov started a preschool program called Gan Yeladim. That afternoon program has grown into a certified preschool'. The Toledo Jewish News (June/July 2025, 'Raizel Shemtov reflects on 35 years at Gan Yeladim Preschool') says 'For over 35 years' and 'When the preschool opened its doors 35 years ago', about 1990, a round count (the same book dates Toledo's Camp Gan Israel, its first children's program, to 1990); the book's stated year is taken. Medium: the two differ. Was 1990 (the 2025 count), source https://cdn.fedweb.org/fed-97/2/June%2520July%25202025%2520TJN-web%25281%2529.pdf.

117711.name: Chabad House-Lubavitch of Greater Toledo
117711.note: Rabbi Shemtov and his family brought Chabad House to Toledo in 1987, at first from their home on Secor Road (Toledo Blade, 2018). Checked: listed as Chabad House of Toledo, Rabbi Yosef Y. Shemtov, in May 1987 (Jewish News). Its own building, 2728 King Road, was dedicated in Sept 2018 (Toledo Blade). lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009 lists it at 4020 Nantucket Drive, Toledo (with the Chai Jewish Student Center at 4230 Rose Garden Drive), before its own building at 2728 King Road (2018). Addresses in the Jewish News: 'CHABAD HOUSE OF TOLEDO, OHIO 750 S. McCord, #105, Holland' (May 15 1987); 'Chabad House of Toledo 2350 Secor Toledo, Ohio 43606' (Dec 14 1990, Feb 22 1991); 'BAIS MENACHEM MENDEL-LUBAVITCH CHABAD HOUSE 4020 Nantucket Drive Toledo, OH 43623' (Sept 7 2002, https://digital.bentley.umich.edu/djnews/djn.2002.09.07.001/53). David M. Noel, 'A History of the Toledo Jewish Community 1895-2006' (p. 155): 'The Chabad movement permanently reached the Toledo community in April 1987 with the arrival of Rabbi Yossi and Raizel Shemtov and their one-year-old son, Mendel'; 'the original Toledo Chabad House was at 2350 Secor Road. In 1997 Chabad relocated to 4020 Nantucket Drive, at the corner of Sylvania Avenue.'
